Alex (product): Quick sync — we need to decide scope for the concurrent actions API: multiple tool calls within one turn, partial ordering, and retry semantics. Customers ask for a fan-out + aggregate pattern a lot.
Sam (eng): +1. Big trade is explicit ordering (user-driven) vs system-optimized parallelism. Explicit DAG gives control but more complexity in surface area.
Priya (ml): For our evals we need determinism. Retries + non-idempotent tools will break reproducibility. We should expose idempotency hints.
Jordan (prodops): Launch criteria thoughts: (1) stable per-action latencies for small tools (<200ms typical), (2) clear billing per action, (3) per-action observability and tracing so customers can debug pipelines.
Miguel (sre): Also need SLOs around cascading failures. Propose default per-action timeout 2000ms and overall request timeout 10000ms, with overrides. Also circuit-breakers for noisy tools.
Sam (eng): Early API sketch: allow an array of "actions" with optional "depends_on", "retry_policy", and "timeout_ms". Example payload:
```
actions: [
  {id: "fetch", tool: "http_get", timeout_ms: 2000},
  {id: "parse", tool: "extract", depends_on: ["fetch"]}
]
```
Priya (ml): Add per-action metadata: idempotency_key or side_effect: "allow" | "forbid" so runtime and customers can reason about retries.
Alex (product): Proposal: support two modes — "orchestrated" (explicit deps) and "optimistic" (system decides parallelism). Default to orchestrated for determinism and easier debugging.
Jordan (prodops): Must be backwards-compatible with current function/tool calling payload shape. Keep wrapper minimal to avoid breaking existing integrators.
Sam (eng): Runtime notes: schedule by topology, batch identical tool calls across requests, and degrade to single-threaded execution if resource constrained. We'll need batching hooks for same-tool parallelism.
Miguel (sre): Retry semantics: default 3 attempts with exponential backoff; allow override per-action. Surface retry_count in logs and metrics. Also record upstream error codes.
Alex (product): Prioritization (MVP vs later): MVP = array actions, depends_on links, per-action timeout, basic retry_policy, and per-action observability. Later = transactional rollback, partial commits, conditional branching DSL.
Priya (ml): Eval metrics for launch: pass correctness on 5 canonical multi-step scenarios, stability across 1k synthetic runs, and clear failure mode mapping for non-idempotent tools.
Jordan (prodops): Docs checklist: examples for fan-out+aggregate, sequential pipelines, conditional branching, and cost explainer showing per-action billing.
Sam (eng): Open question: streaming partial results vs only final aggregate. Streaming each completed action back to the client would improve UX for long-running tools. I vote yes.
Alex (product): Agree — streaming partial outputs is high-value. Add to criteria if it's feasible without large infra changes.
Priya (ml): Security note: enforce tool-level capability tokens. When fan-out reaches external endpoints, ensure no cross-tenant leakage and proper vaulted credentials.
Miguel (sre): Infra work: emit metrics per action_id: latency_ms, error_rate, retry_count. New alert rules for abnormal retry spikes and high aggregation latencies.
Alex (product): Next steps: Sam to draft API spec + example payloads; Priya to draft eval plan and idempotency tests; Jordan to draft launch checklist and docs; Miguel to list telemetry/alert changes. Reconvene Thursday. :rocket:
Jordan (prodops): I'll create the tracking epic and link to quarterly roadmap.
deploy-bot: RFC created: https://redwood/notes/concurrent-actions-rfc
Alex (product): Thanks — please add any immediate blockers in the epic.
